chapter.title: The President’s Other Appointment
chapter.goal: Steve wants to stop the swap of the President.

c7_gate.coach: Three of you today: Steve, Stephen and Pell. Press Q to switch between them.
c7_gate.objective: Get two Steves and a mail carrier into the signing. Watch the President.
changes: U-cast (no new gate_guard voice: Rook’s copy works the gate)
notes: C14 asked for a new gate_guard role. Rook’s copy runs the FBI liaison at the event (plot), so he works the checkpoint instead. No new voice is needed.
badge and post become rows puzzles (drop the case boards). truck stays a choice with a new prompt.
Ward’s ribbon burn on her left wrist is the clue that solves c7_swap.map. Keep ‘left wrist’ in every mention.
context: steve|Sentinel Point. An old antenna field in the fog north of town, flags on every mast, and the President of the United States due at noon.

badge.title: The checkpoint
badge.goal: Get the sound truck, and Steve, through the gate.
badge.background: Halcyon’s sound truck needs a crew to get in. Stephen still has a Halcyon crew pass. Steve has no pass, Dad’s tape of the ninth-night tone in his pocket, and his face on every wanted poster.
lead: c7_gate.in.01
steve|My face is on every poster in the county. So is yours.
stephen|Then one of us should hide. I vote you.
stephen|The gate card has three windows. Red at 11:10 is for deliveries on foot. No vehicles at all.
stephen|Gold at 11:50 is for the signers. The President’s guards search every vehicle with dogs.
stephen|Blue at 11:30 is for crew trucks. The guard scans the driver’s pass. If it shows green, the truck rolls through.
steve|And I have no pass at all. So the guard can’t be allowed to see me.
badge.prompt: Pick the gate window, the driver, and where Steve rides.
badge.instruction: Gate card. Red 11:10: on foot only, no vehicles. Blue 11:30: crew trucks roll through if the driver’s pass scans green. Gold 11:50: dogs search every vehicle. Stephen has a crew pass. Steve has none.
hints: The tape has to go in with the truck. Which window lets a truck in without a search?
At that window the guard only looks at the driver. Who has a pass that scans green?
The man with no pass must stay out of the guard’s sight. Where in the truck can he hide?

lines.direction: at the gate, holding up a wanted poster

lines: stephen|I get that a lot. Scan me.
rook_copy|Saren’s hunter. Any luck?
stephen|He’s very close. I can feel it.
c7_gate.badge.01
badge.finding: steve|Blue window, 11:30. Stephen drove, his pass scanned green, and I rode under the sound desk. Rook’s copy waved us through and wished Stephen luck finding me.

post.title: Accord mail
post.goal: Get the letter into the President’s own hand, and a receipt back.
post.background: Pell carries a registered letter for President Ward. Registered mail must go into her own hand, and Pell always brings back a receipt with her signature on it.
lead: c7_gate.in.02
pell|Registered mail goes into the addressee’s own hand. Nobody else may sign for her.
pell|The press desk only stamps handouts for reporters. The stage door only signs for scenery.
pell|The delegation clerk can call the President to her hatch in person.
pell|She signs the white sheet, and her pen presses through to the yellow carbon underneath. The white sheet stays with her.
post.prompt: Pick the hatch, and the receipt Pell brings back.
post.instruction: Press desk: stamps handouts for reporters. Stage door: signs for scenery. Delegation hatch: the clerk can call the President herself. The President signs the white sheet, and her pen presses through to the yellow carbon. The white sheet stays with her.
hints: The letter must reach the President’s own hand. Which hatch can bring her there?
The white sheet stays with the President. Pell needs a receipt he can carry away.
Look for the sheet that carries her signature, pressed through from the sheet above.
lines: c7_gate.post.01
c7_gate.post.02
ward|Ribbon burn on my left wrist, from the accord folder. My first wound in office.

lines.new: pell|Eleven fifty-four. Left wrist, bandaged. Noted for the record.
lines.direction: writing on the counterfoil, then saluting

post.finding: steve|Pell put the letter into Ward’s own hand at the delegation hatch at 11:54 and came back with the yellow carbon. And a note for the record: left wrist, bandaged. A fresh ribbon burn.

truck.title: Halcyon broadcast truck
truck.goal: Prove the back-fence speakers are working.
truck.background: Halcyon’s truck runs every speaker on the site, and Steve needs every one of them. The back fence failed its sound check. The fence is 170 meters from the desk, and sound travels 340 meters in one second.

lead.new: steve|I climbed out from under the sound desk, tripped over a cable and fell straight into the shot of a live television camera.

lead: c7_gate.truck.01

lead.text: Evelyn Shaw. I ran the sound stage for Meridian, back when it had a budget. Stay off the cables.

lead: shaw|The back fence failed the check. Sound crosses three hundred and forty meters in a second, and the fence is a hundred and seventy meters out. Tell me what it actually heard.
shaw|The camera monitor shows the click the moment it leaves this desk.
shaw|The stage van shows the television feed. That runs two seconds late, because of the satellite.
truck.prompt: Three strips in the truck show the same test click. Which strip shows what the fence heard?
options: Fence line, in the truck: 0.5 seconds

wrong.0: That’s the click leaving the desk. Sound needs some time to cover 170 meters.
wrong.1: Two seconds is the satellite delay on the television feed, not the fence.

hints: Sound is not instant. How far away is the fence?
In one second sound goes 340 meters. The fence is half that far.
The satellite delay belongs to the television, not the fence. Which strip shows the time sound needs for 170 meters?
lines: shaw|Half a second. Good ears. Who taught you?
steve|My dad.
truck.finding: steve|Sound covers 170 meters in half a second. The fence-line strip in the Halcyon truck shows the click at 0.5 s, so the fence hears the desk. Every speaker on the site is mine.

recap: steve|We were in. Stephen as a loyal asset, Pell as the mail, and me at the sound desk with Dad’s tape of the ninth-night tone.
steve|Ward signed for Pell’s letter at 11:54, with a fresh bandage on her left wrist. The public ceremony starts at 11:58.
outro: steve|If they swap her, it happens between the hatch and the podium.
stephen|So we watch the hatch. I’m very good at being looked at.

outro.new: steve|In the fog between the antennas, an old woman was walking a dog. Mrs. Penhallow. Miles from her pier, again.

lines: steve|Can you see the trucks from here? I can barely see my own feet.
stephen|Good. Fog is very flattering. Nobody looks like a wanted poster in fog.
steve|Dad used to say fog makes every sound feel closer.
stephen|He said it on the boat, every summer. I remember that one. I think I do.
stephen|I had two croissants from Gus this morning. He gave me a third one for free.
steve|He thinks you’re me, Stephen. My face is on every poster.
stephen|He said the poster doesn’t do me justice. He’s right, you know.
steve|Rook’s copy wished you luck finding me.
stephen|I told him the truth. You’re very close. You’re under the sound desk.
steve|Please stop enjoying this so much.
stephen|I can’t. This is the most fun I’ve had in my whole short life.
steve|Who is looking after Biscuit today?
pell|The Sheriff’s neighbor. I left written instructions. Four pages, with diagrams.
steve|Four pages, for one beagle?
pell|She is a very important beagle. She has a schedule.
pell|Dale’s route has two hundred and twelve mailboxes. I know every one of them.
steve|Do you actually like the work?
pell|I like the dogs, and the people who say thank you. Mostly the dogs.
rook_copy|The coffee in the press tent is terrible. I’ve had four cups.
stephen|You don’t seem to mind it very much.
rook_copy|Rook takes his coffee black. I keep putting sugar in mine. I don’t know why.

rook_copy.topic: The one he was made from
lines: rook_copy|Do you ever think about him? The one you were made from?
stephen|Every single day. He snores, apparently.
rook_copy|I wonder if mine dreams. Down there, in the cold.
ward|Is it always this foggy up here?
pell|Most mornings, Madam President. The fishermen say the fog keeps the town quiet.
ward|I grew up in Kansas. I could get used to quiet.
shaw|This truck is older than you are. I rewired half of it myself.
steve|It still sounds good, though.
shaw|Of course it does. I have good ears too. Mine are just older.
shaw|Before this, I built explosions for the movies. Six films, and never one real fire.
steve|And now you run sound checks in the fog?
shaw|The government pays worse. But the sandwiches are better.

c7_swap.objective: Find the real President, then make every copy on the site give itself away.
notes: Saren speaks through Stephen’s earpiece (delivery radio). He has not met Steve before.
Wen’s introduction and the notebook lines move here from c7_gate (C15). Shaw’s line ends the chapter.
The tone reasoning in the intro uses what the player has seen: the ninth-night processions (Chapters 1 and 3) and Frank’s reels (Chapter 5). It does not point at Mrs. Penhallow.
context: steve|Every ninth night, when the bay sounds that tone, every copy near Bellwether walks to the water. Dad taped it.
steve|If it played on every speaker at once, every copy on the site would answer it at once. In front of everybody.

intro.direction: through Stephen’s earpiece, which Stephen holds out to Steve

map.title: Event monitor
map.goal: Work out which Ward is real, and where the real one went.
map.background: Iris told Steve that the President’s own doctor scanned her at a checkup weeks ago. A copy made from that scan knows nothing about this morning. This morning Ward burned her left wrist, and Pell wrote down the bandage at 11:54.
lead: stephen|I just gave the press a short interview. They loved me. Now, four feeds and one President. Possibly two.
steve|Iris said Ward’s own doctor scanned her weeks ago. A copy made back then can’t know about this morning.
stephen|And this morning she burned her left wrist on the folder. Pell wrote it down. Left wrist, bandaged.
stephen|Podium camera. The woman at the lectern just waved. Her left wrist is bare.
stephen|Stair camera. The doctor is helping a patient down the east stair. Her left wrist is bandaged.
stephen|The east stair only goes to one door, into the service tunnel. And the lift went down empty.
map.prompt: Which woman is the real President, and where did she go?

board.instruction: Use the bandage to tell the two Wards apart, then find where the real one went.
evidence: The President’s doctor scanned her weeks ago, so a copy made then has no injury from this morning.
At 11:54 Ward signed for Pell’s letter with a fresh bandage on her left wrist.
Podium camera, 11:57: the woman at the lectern waves, and her left wrist is bare.
Stair camera, 11:56: the doctor helps a patient with a bandaged left wrist down the east stair.
The east stair leads only to the service tunnel, and the lift went down with nobody in it.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each question.
slots: Who was made from the old scan?
Which way did the doctor take her?

board.wrong_text: Stephen squints at the feeds. One of these cards is on the wrong question.

hints: What happened to Ward this morning that a scan from weeks ago could not know?
Ward burned her left wrist this morning. Check each woman’s left wrist.
Follow the woman with the bandage. The lift carried nobody, so look at where the stair camera saw her.
lines: c7_swap.map.01

lines.new: saren|Mr. Mercer, the sound desk is a very small room.

map.finding: steve|The woman at the lectern has a bare wrist, so she was made from the old scan. The real Ward, with this morning’s bandage, went down the east stair with the physician into the service tunnel. June and Iris are going after her.

bus.title: Sound desk routing
bus.goal: Send the tone to every speaker on the site, but not to the television feed.
bus.background: Steve has Dad’s tone cued at the sound desk. It must reach the lectern and the back fence, but not the press van, which feeds the national broadcast. June needs a private line back to Steve and Stephen.
lead: steve|Dad’s tape. Cued, and ready.
shaw|Three sends. Amber reaches the lectern and the press van. Green reaches the back fence and the service steps.
shaw|Blue reaches the lectern, the back fence and the service steps.
shaw|The press van feeds the national broadcast. Keep your tone off it, or every copy watching at home hears it too.
shaw|For June’s reply, three returns. Copper goes to you, Stephen and the lectern speaker.
shaw|Slate goes to you and Stephen. Pearl goes to you alone.
steve|June’s reply is for Stephen and me. Nobody else.
bus.prompt: Pick the send for the tone, and the return for June’s reply.
bus.instruction: The tone must reach the lectern and the back fence, but not the press van. June’s reply must reach Steve and Stephen, and nobody else. Sends: Amber goes to the lectern and the press van. Blue goes to the lectern, back fence and service steps. Green goes to the back fence and service steps. Returns: Copper goes to Steve, Stephen and the lectern. Slate goes to Steve and Stephen. Pearl goes to Steve alone.
hints: Do one row at a time. Start with where the tone must go.
The tone needs the lectern and the fence. One send misses the lectern, and one reaches the press van.
For June’s reply, count who hears each return. One reaches too many people, and one leaves Stephen out.
lines: c7_swap.bus.01
bus.finding: steve|The tone goes out on Blue: the lectern, the back fence and the service steps, but not the press van. June’s reply comes back on Slate, to Stephen and me alone.

tone.title: Ceremony cue
tone.goal: Play the tone at the one moment that works.
tone.background: When the tone plays, every copy on the site will stop and turn toward the sea. June and Iris must reach the real Ward first, or the crew will move her. The tone must also finish before the anthem starts.

lead.new: calder|Service tunnel. We see them. Give us a few seconds.
calder|The team gets to the patient at 11:58 and fourteen seconds. Not one second sooner.

lead: shaw|The speakers switch to the anthem at eighteen seconds past. Your tone runs two seconds. It has to finish before then.
tone.prompt: June and Iris reach the real Ward at 11:58:14. The speakers switch to the anthem at 11:58:18. The tone lasts two seconds. When should Steve start it?

wrong.0: June and Iris don’t reach the patient until :14. The crew would move her the moment the copies turned.
wrong.2: Two seconds from :17 runs past :18, into the anthem. The tone would be cut off.

hints: Too early, and the crew moves Ward. Too late, and the anthem cuts off the tone.
June and Iris reach Ward at :14. The tone has to start after that.
Count two seconds forward from each choice. Which start is after :14 and still ends by :18?

lines.new: steve|Fourteen people stopped in the fog and turned toward the sea.

lines: c7_swap.tone.01
tone.finding: steve|At 11:58:15 Dad’s tone went out on every site speaker. Fourteen people stopped and turned toward the sea, the woman at the microphone among them. June and Iris had the real President.

recap: steve|Fourteen copies turned toward the sea at once, in front of everyone who mattered. The real President was in a service tunnel, with a bandaged wrist and June Calder.
steve|Iris told me later that the tone pulled at her too. She held on to June’s sleeve and counted Sunday dinners until it passed.
steve|Rook’s copy slipped away into the fog. Before he went, he asked me one thing.

outro.new: steve|An hour later, in a locked room under the array, the President of the United States thanked me.

outro.text: Thank you, Mr. Mercer. Their Prefect wants one thing from us by the ninth night. Our space-fold engine.
Lin Wen. I was the other side’s engineer at Sentinel Point, nine years ago. Helen wrote this? Where is she?
outro.direction: seeing the notebook in Steve’s hand

outro.text: This page... Madam President. He should hear it from us.

outro: ward|Now we owe you an explanation.
c7_swap.next: Chapter 8: the flashback to Sentinel Point, nine years ago (p_meeting).

lines: steve|What did the press ask you?
stephen|My favorite food. I said Sunday dinner at La Marea. Then I wasn’t sure whose memory that was.
steve|It belongs to both of us. It was a good answer.
stephen|My hands are shaking. Are yours shaking too?
steve|They’ve been shaking since six this morning.
stephen|Good. I was worried it was only me.
shaw|The last time I sat at a desk out here, four generals stood behind me.
steve|Were they as nervous as I am?
shaw|Less. Breathe, Mercer. The tape won’t play any faster if you hold your breath.
shaw|Your father’s tape is in good shape. Who stored it?
steve|He did. Cool and dry, and labeled in pencil. He labeled everything.
shaw|Then I would have hired him in a heartbeat.

lines.new: calder|Iris is right beside me. She’s counting her steps out loud.

lines: steve|Is she all right down there?

lines.new: calder|She says she’s fine. She says it the way you always do.
